body:
I have done some testing and I have reproduced the issue. I have traced its introduction to the Godot 4.5 dev4 build from when macOS embedded support was first added. I could not reproduce the bug at commit 9a09fc3 (one commit before macOS embedded support was added) and before. I encountered a runtime error ("ERROR: DisplayServerEmbedded is not initialized.") from commit 00e1fde onwards up to the commit before 9290ade, so the crash was not able to be encountered. The first commit I encountered the crash was commit 9290ade. It appears that this has been an issue from around when macOS embedded support was first added.

I tested the builds on a M1 Pro, macOS 26.6.2. I tested with the default renderer driver on each version/commit.

I am not that familiar with the codebase yet, but after looking into it further, it appears that --embedded was not intended to be called directly from the command line rather a flag used by the editor when setting up game embedding in the game view tab. That is why the EngineDebugger::get_singleton() calls were unguarded as the embedded display server was only meant to be used in the editor. You may be thinking of --headless instead of --embedded to run the project without a window of its own. Regardless, I am thinking of making a commit that checks if the EngineDebugger singleton exists when constructing the embedded macos display server as a proxy to check if the process is being created from the editor or directly by the command line. If the EngineDebugger singleton is NULL, then the process was likely called from the command line and there could be a warning printed to not use the --embedded flag directly and godot exits early that avoids a crash.

I've implemented the fix and it works like expected on my mac now, but the PR was rejected because it was created through AI agent interface and I added AI Agent Disclosure there

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123721

the code change is valid and tested though, I'm using it locally for a few days now
so if anyone picks it up please take a look at the PR, it could be used as is
